summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes EEG-AS, a framework that treats EEG foundation model deployment as an instance-level algorithm selection problem to overcome the limitations of using a single best solver. It utilizes an anchor model and latent embeddings to reconstruct the prediction behaviors (tokens) of other models in a portfolio without executing them. Evaluation across seven public EEG benchmarks shows that EEG-AS significantly improves selection accuracy and narrows the gap between the single best solver and the theoretical oracle upper bound.

headline_results: Average accuracy increased from 53.7% (SBS) to 66.9% (EEG-AS).
Closed 44% of the gap between SBS and the Oracle (VBS).

key_points: Proposed EEG-AS to bridge the gap between the Single Best Solver (SBS) and the Virtual Best Solver (VBS).
Uses a conditional token predictor to reconstruct the behaviors of multiple FMs from a single anchor model's output.
Demonstrated performance gains across 7 diverse EEG benchmarks, improving average accuracy from 53.7% to 66.9%.
limitations: Dependence on the quality of the anchor model for behavior reconstruction.
Computational overhead of the selection framework compared to a single model.

method.architecture: Conditional Token Predictor and Token-based Model Selector using cross-attention.
method.finetuning: Joint optimization of the predictor and selector on benchmark tasks.
method.objective: Joint loss combining pairwise logistic ranking loss for selection and MSE for token reconstruction.
method.pretraining: Pretrained on privileged information (prediction tokens from the full portfolio).

summary.one_liner: An instance-level algorithm selection framework that adaptively chooses the best EEG foundation model for each sample by reconstructing model behaviors from a single anchor model.
summary.title: EEG-AS: Instance-Level Foundation Model Selection for EEG Foundation Models via Behavior Reconstruction
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a behavior reconstruction mechanism using privileged information to select the optimal EEG foundation model per instance without requiring full inference of the entire portfolio.

papers.title: EEG-AS: Instance-Level Foundation Model Selection for EEG Foundation Models via Behavior Reconstruction

reasons: Explicitly targets the selection and adaptive deployment of multiple EEG foundation models.
Focuses on an instance-level algorithm selection framework specifically for EEG-FMs.
Utilizes latent EEG embeddings from foundation models to characterize neural activity.

summary.detailed_summary: SleepFM-2 is a foundation model pretrained on 235,865 multimodal polysomnography (PSG) recordings using a combination of masked autoencoding and leave-one-out contrastive learning. It employs a two-stage transformer architecture with 1-second temporal patching and channel-region embeddings to capture fine-grained physiological signals across brain, heart, muscle, and respiratory systems. The model demonstrates strong transferability, predicting 215 incident disease phenotypes and generalizing to wearable sensors like headband EEG and wrist accelerometry using a frozen encoder.

headline_results: C-index >= 0.75 for 215 incident disease phenotypes
Outperformed SleepFM and 480-feature baseline

key_points: New EEG foundation model: SleepFM-2 is pretrained on over two million hours of multimodal PSG data from 24 cohorts.
Method novelty: Combines masked autoencoding with a leave-one-out contrastive objective to learn representations across brain, heart, muscle, and respiratory signals.
Strong evidence: Predicts 215 incident disease phenotypes (C-index >= 0.75) and transfers to non-PSG sensors including in-ear EEG and wrist PPG.
limitations: Requires an engineered bridge to transfer to accelerometry as it shares no channels with PSG.
A significant portion of learned features in the latent space do not align with known labeled domains.
Pretraining depends on high-cost clinical PSG recordings.

method.architecture: Two-stage transformer encoder with 1-second temporal patches and channel-region embeddings.
method.finetuning: Frozen encoder with light task-specific heads.
method.objective: Joint Masked Autoencoding (MAE) and Leave-One-Out Contrastive (LOO-CL) loss.
method.pretraining: Pretrained on 235,865 recordings with a 55% masking rate using temporal-block, channel-block, and random masking.

summary.one_liner: A multimodal sleep foundation model pretrained on 2 million hours of PSG that transfers to diverse clinical tasks, subjective reports, and wearable sensors.
summary.title: Learning transferable human physiology from two million hours of sleep with SleepFM-2
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a multimodal sleep foundation model that learns a transferable representation of human health capable of generalizing from clinical PSG to wearable sensors and subjective sleep experiences.

papers.title: Learning transferable human physiology from two million hours of sleep with SleepFM-2

reasons: Explicitly identifies SleepFM-2 as a 'sleep foundation model' pretrained on a massive dataset of 235,865 PSG recordings.
Demonstrates broad transferability of the frozen encoder to various EEG modalities, including wakeful, headband, and in-ear EEG.
Focuses on creating a transferable representation of human physiology across diverse clinical tasks, sensors, and phenotypes.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes iBrain, a foundation model that integrates signal-specific encoders with a shared spatiotemporal Transformer backbone to learn from both iEEG and intracortical spikes. Unlike previous models that focus on a single recording paradigm, iBrain uses masked reconstruction and channel-view alignment to create a shared representation space for heterogeneous signals. Evaluation on eight benchmarks across motor decoding and language perception shows that joint pretraining outperforms single-signal baselines on most tasks.

headline_results: Outperformed baselines on 7 out of 8 benchmarks
Significant improvement in iEEG Volume decoding AUC from 0.75 to 0.89

key_points: New EEG foundation model: iBrain jointly learns from iEEG and intracortical spiking activity to create a unified representation of brain dynamics across scales.
Employs a shared spatiotemporal Transformer backbone with signal-specific encoders and a dual pretraining objective of masked reconstruction and channel-view alignment.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on 7 out of 8 benchmarks spanning motor decoding and language-related tasks, demonstrating the benefit of joint pretraining.
limitations: Did not achieve the best result on the Perich T-RT random-target reaching benchmark.
Evaluation is limited to invasive recordings, leaving the integration of non-invasive EEG unexplored.
The model's performance on extremely rare recording types is not detailed.

method.architecture: Signal-specific encoders for iEEG waveform patches and binned spike counts, followed by a 6-layer shared spatiotemporal Transformer backbone.
method.finetuning: Task-specific prediction heads are added to the frozen or unfrozen backbone for downstream decoding tasks.
method.objective: Masked signal reconstruction (50% masking) and channel-view alignment using a cosine similarity objective on pooled representations of channel subsets.
method.pretraining: Joint pretraining on iEEG (3,950 hours) and spiking activity (3,209 hours) to learn a shared representation space.

summary.one_liner: iBrain is a unified foundation model that jointly learns from heterogeneous invasive neural recordings, including iEEG and intracortical spiking activity.
summary.title: iBrain: A Unified Foundation Model Reading the Brain from Surface to Spikes
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces the first foundation model to jointly pretrain on heterogeneous invasive neural recordings (iEEG and spiking activity) using a shared spatiotemporal backbone.

papers.title: iBrain: A Unified Foundation Model Reading the Brain from Surface to Spikes

reasons: Explicitly introduces iBrain as a 'unified foundation model' for iEEG and spiking activity.
Pretrained on a large-scale dataset of over 7,000 hours of neural recordings.
Demonstrates transferability and data efficiency across diverse recording settings and downstream tasks.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes BRIDGE-EEG, a framework that maps diverse EEG recordings to a device-agnostic 62-channel time-frequency representation to enable a shared backbone. It utilizes an SE-ResNet18 teacher pretrained via SimCLR on five heterogeneous datasets, which is then compressed into SE-ResNet8 and SE-ResNet4 students through task-agnostic and task-specific distillation. Evaluation across six benchmarks shows that these compact models match or exceed the performance of foundation models 10-1,000x larger in abnormality detection and emotion recognition, while significantly reducing energy consumption on edge hardware.

headline_results: Students match or exceed FMs 10-1,000x larger in abnormality and emotion tasks
Up to 3.0x lower energy per inference on edge devices

key_points: Method for efficient EEG deployment: Combines self-supervised pretraining with knowledge distillation to create compact models (down to 0.48M parameters).
High efficiency: Achieves up to 3.0x lower energy per inference on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano compared to larger models.
Strong transfer: Maintains accuracy comparable to foundation models 10-1,000x larger for abnormality detection and emotion recognition.
limitations: A representation gap remains for motor imagery tasks, suggesting a need for greater pretraining diversity.
The unified preprocessing maps all data to a fixed 62-channel representation, which may lose some original signal nuances.
Evaluation is limited to specific benchmarks and does not cover all possible EEG applications.

method.architecture: SE-ResNet (Teacher: ResNet18, Students: ResNet8/4)
method.objective: SimCLR contrastive loss
method.pretraining: Multi-dataset self-supervised pretraining on unlabeled EEG

summary.one_liner: A pipeline for compressing self-supervised pretrained EEG models into compact students for efficient edge deployment without sacrificing significant accuracy.
summary.title: BRIDGE-EEG: Bridging Self-Supervised Pretraining and Efficient Deployment for Cross-Dataset EEG Classification
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a three-stage pipeline combining unified preprocessing, SimCLR pretraining on heterogeneous data, and knowledge distillation to enable high-performance EEG classification on resource-constrained hardware.

papers.title: BRIDGE-EEG: Bridging Self-Supervised Pretraining and Efficient Deployment for Cross-Dataset EEG Classification

reasons: Explicitly frames the work as addressing the computational costs of EEG foundation models for edge deployment.
Utilizes large-scale self-supervised pretraining (SimCLR) on five heterogeneous datasets to learn general EEG representations.
Focuses on the EEG-FM ecosystem by developing a compression/distillation pipeline to preserve pretrained representation benefits.
Evaluates the resulting models across multiple diverse benchmarks including abnormality detection, motor imagery, and emotion recognition.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes MAPA, a masked autoencoder designed for intracranial EEG (iEEG) that addresses the challenge of heterogeneous electrode placement across subjects. It introduces a novel combination of anatomical region embeddings and relative positional encodings (RoPE) within a ViT-based architecture to capture shared spatial properties of the brain. Evaluation on the Neuroprobe benchmark demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across within-session, cross-session, and cross-subject regimes, significantly reducing the labeled data required for new subjects.

headline_results: SOTA performance in within-session, cross-session, and cross-subject regimes
21x reduction in labeled data required for cross-subject transfer

key_points: New EEG foundation model: MAPA uses a masked autoencoder architecture with anatomical and relative positional encodings to learn transferable iEEG representations.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on the Neuroprobe benchmark across all evaluation regimes, including cross-subject transfer.
Demonstrates extreme sample efficiency, requiring ~21x fewer labeled trials (164 vs 3,500) to reach baseline accuracy in cross-subject decoding.
limitations: Pretraining data is limited to 7 subjects from a single dataset.
Relies on the availability of anatomical region labels from a standard brain atlas.
Evaluation is primarily focused on the Neuroprobe benchmark.
The encoder is kept frozen during downstream evaluation.

method.architecture: ViT-Small encoder and a smaller ViT decoder
method.finetuning: Linear probing with a frozen encoder on downstream tasks
method.objective: Masked reconstruction of frequency bins using MSE loss
method.pretraining: Pretrained on 27.9 hours of iEEG data using anatomical region embeddings and rotary position embeddings (RoPE)

summary.one_liner: MAPA is a masked autoencoder for iEEG that uses anatomical and relative positional encodings to enable cross-subject transfer and high sample efficiency.
summary.title: Pretraining for Sample-Efficient Neural Interfaces
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a masked autoencoder for iEEG that combines anatomical region embeddings and relative positional encodings to learn subject-agnostic neural representations.

papers.title: Pretraining for Sample-Efficient Neural Interfaces

reasons: Proposes MAPA, a self-supervised pretrained model for iEEG to learn general neural representations.
Explicitly targets broad transfer across unseen subjects and various tasks.
Demonstrates the ability to scale across heterogeneous recordings to create reusable representations.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes MANAS-2, which combines a Raw-Band Hybrid (RBH) masked autoencoder with Constrained Reconstruction (ConRec), a regularizer that penalizes RMS-energy jumps in the reconstructed temporal signal. Unlike typical MAEs that focus solely on pointwise error, ConRec biases the encoder toward capturing oscillatory-envelope information. Evaluation across seven held-out datasets shows significant improvements in spectral power recovery and downstream knowledge-transfer tasks compared to existing EEG foundation models.

headline_results: Increased six-band spectral power recovery R^2 from 0.860 to 0.906
Outperformed REVE, BIOT, and LaBraM on most downstream transfer tasks

key_points: New EEG foundation model: MANAS-2 utilizes a Raw-Band Hybrid architecture and a novel ConRec regularizer to enhance spectral representation.
Method novelty: ConRec improves latent organization by penalizing RMS-energy jumps in the temporal decoder output, independent of explicit spectral targets.
Strong evidence: Outperforms leading models on most downstream transfer tasks and increases six-band spectral power recovery from R^2=0.860 to 0.906.
limitations: The effect of ConRec on the aperiodic exponent was minimal, suggesting it primarily targets oscillatory-envelope information.
The paper does not provide the specific scale of the pretraining corpus used for MANAS-2.
Downstream evaluation was performed using frozen representations, leaving the potential gains of full fine-tuning unexplored.

method.architecture: Transformer-based masked autoencoder using a Raw-Band Hybrid (RBH) architecture with a shared encoder and separate temporal and spectral decoders.
method.finetuning: Frozen representation learning with linear ridge probes (LP-AVG) for downstream tasks.
method.objective: Joint temporal reconstruction, spectral band target prediction (6 bands), and the ConRec RMS-energy regularizer.
method.pretraining: Masked autoencoding on EEG data using temporal-patch tokenization.

summary.one_liner: An EEG foundation model that uses a physics-motivated RMS-energy constraint on reconstructed waveforms to improve the spectral organization and transferability of latent representations.
summary.title: MANAS-2: Constrained Reconstruction for EEG Foundation Models
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces Constrained Reconstruction (ConRec), a physics-motivated temporal regularizer that shapes the encoder's latent space by imposing local energy constraints on the reconstructed waveform.

papers.title: MANAS-2: Constrained Reconstruction for EEG Foundation Models

reasons: Explicitly introduces MANAS-2 as a new EEG foundation model.
Focuses on creating transferable latent representations evaluated across seven held-out EEG datasets.
Directly compares performance against other leading EEG Foundation Models on downstream knowledge-transfer tasks.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes EEG-Xplain, a unified framework designed to decode the 'black-box' nature of heterogeneous EEG foundation models like BIOT, LaBraM, and EEGMamba. It integrates gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based attribution methods to analyze model behavior across spatial, temporal, and frequency domains, while introducing a population-level fidelity evaluation using Area Over the Perturbation Curve (AOPC). The framework further employs LLMs to translate structured attribution data into natural-language clinical reports, with validation on the Mumtaz2016 and TUAB datasets showing consistency with neurophysiological markers.

headline_results: Demonstrated consistency between model attributions and established neurophysiological markers.
Validated attribution fidelity using AOPC across multiple foundation model architectures.

key_points: Method for EEG-FM interpretability: Proposes a unified framework to analyze spatial, temporal, and frequency-domain attributions across diverse architectures like Transformers and Mamba.
Fidelity-driven validation: Implements a population-level evaluation using AOPC to ensure attribution results are causally consistent with model decisions.
Neuro-symbolic reasoning: Bridges the gap between low-level heatmaps and clinical logic by using LLMs to generate natural-language diagnostic reports.
limitations: Preliminary nature of the neuro-symbolic reasoning pathway using LLMs for clinical report generation.
Potential for models to rely on artifacts or spurious patterns, which the framework identifies but cannot inherently fix.
Computational overhead associated with perturbation-based attribution methods like SHAP and LIME.

method.architecture: Unified attribution interface supporting gradient-based (IG, Gradient-SHAP), perturbation-based (Occlusion, SHAP, LIME), and activation-based (Grad-CAM) methods.
method.objective: Fidelity evaluation via Area Over the Perturbation Curve (AOPC) and LLM-based semantic translation.

summary.one_liner: A unified attribution framework for interpreting EEG foundation models across spatial, temporal, and frequency dimensions, integrating LLMs for clinical report generation.
summary.title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a unified cross-architecture attribution framework that distills high-dimensional EEG-FM representations into multi-dimensional physical evidence and translates them into semantic clinical reports via LLMs.

papers.title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models

reasons: Explicitly targets EEG foundation models such as BIOT, LaBraM, and EEGMamba.
Proposes a unified attribution framework specifically for interpreting EEG-FM behavior.
Contributes to the EEG-FM ecosystem by providing a standardized approach for evaluating interpretability and physiological plausibility.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes augmenting the CBraMod foundation model with cross-depth Attention Residuals (AttnRes) and soft-routed expert banks to improve downstream EEG decoding. Unlike standard full fine-tuning, these modules allow the model to aggregate features from multiple depths and apply input-dependent transformations. Evaluation across four datasets (FACED, ISRUC, SEED-V, and PhysioNet-MI) reveals that these additions produce dataset-dependent results with significant computational overhead, rather than consistent performance gains.

headline_results: Balanced Accuracy (BA) changes ranged from -1.27 (PhysioNet-MI) to +1.27 (ISRUC).
AttnRes alone improved performance in 3 out of 4 datasets.
Runtime increased by 2.41-3.04x and memory by 1.86-2.85x.

key_points: Method study on EEG foundation model fine-tuning: evaluates whether adding AttnRes and soft-routed experts improves CBraMod over standard full fine-tuning.
Findings show heterogeneous results across tasks, with gains in sleep staging (ISRUC) but losses in motor imagery (PhysioNet-MI).
The proposed augmentations significantly increase runtime (up to 3.04x) and memory (up to 2.85x) usage.
limitations: Limited to a single backbone (CBraMod).
Only one protocol per dataset was tested.
Results based on only three random seeds.
SEED-V dataset is not subject-disjoint.
Lack of a parameter-matched dense control for the expert-stage comparison.

method.architecture: CBraMod backbone augmented with cross-depth Attention Residuals (weighted sum of previous block outputs) and soft-routed expert banks (MLPs with input-dependent routing).
method.finetuning: Full fine-tuning of the backbone and training of the added AttnRes and expert modules.
method.objective: Downstream classification (Emotion, Sleep staging, Motor imagery).
method.pretraining: Uses pretrained CBraMod weights.

summary.one_liner: Investigates the impact of cross-depth aggregation and soft-routed experts on the fine-tuning of the CBraMod EEG foundation model.
summary.title: Dataset-Dependent Effects of Cross-Depth Aggregation and Soft-Routed Experts in EEG Foundation Model Fine-Tuning
summary.unique_contribution: Demonstrates that adding cross-depth aggregation and expert routing to a fully trainable EEG foundation model yields inconsistent, dataset-dependent performance gains at a high computational cost.

papers.title: Dataset-Dependent Effects of Cross-Depth Aggregation and Soft-Routed Experts in EEG Foundation Model Fine-Tuning

reasons: Explicitly focuses on 'EEG foundation model fine-tuning'
Evaluates adaptation strategies for an existing EEG-FM (CBraMod)
Tests the model across multiple EEG datasets to analyze fine-tuning effects

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes iMINDBench, a benchmark spanning 15 language, auditory, and visual decoding tasks across three naturalistic movie-watching iEEG datasets. It introduces standardized preprocessing tracks (Multi-STFT and Waveform) and fixed evaluation splits to isolate model improvements from preprocessing gains. Results show that while pretrained models generally outperform baselines, strong spectral baselines remain competitive, and scaling supervised data across institutions provides limited gains.

headline_results: Pretrained systems generally outperform non-pretrained baselines within tracks.
Strong spectral baselines (Multi-STFT) remain competitive with pretrained waveform systems.
Scaling supervised data across institutions yields small or task-dependent gains.

key_points: Benchmark for iEEG decoding: Evaluates models across 15 tasks and three multi-institution datasets using standardized preprocessing tracks.
Preprocessing impact: Demonstrates that strong spectral baselines are competitive with pretrained waveform systems, highlighting the role of input representation.
Scaling limitations: Finds that adding supervised data from other subjects or institutions yields only small or task-dependent improvements over within-session training.
limitations: Many evaluation units remain near chance performance in the Challenge subset.
Limited gains observed when scaling supervised data across institutions.
Performance is strongly influenced by preprocessing choices.
Dataset scale and electrode coverage are heterogeneous across the three institutions.

method.architecture: Benchmark framework evaluating various decoders (Logistic Regression, MLP, CNN, PopT-v2, HTNet, BaRISTA, DIVER-1).
method.finetuning: Supervised training across three scaling domains: within-session, within-dataset, and multi-dataset.
method.objective: Neural decoding of naturalistic stimuli.
method.pretraining: Evaluates pretrained iEEG models against non-pretrained baselines.

summary.one_liner: A multi-institution iEEG benchmark for neural decoding that standardizes preprocessing and evaluation across 15 tasks and three datasets.
summary.title: iMINDBench: iEEG Multi-Institution Neural Decoding Benchmark
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces iMINDBench, a standardized framework for evaluating iEEG decoding models across multiple institutions and tasks while controlling for preprocessing effects.

papers.title: iMINDBench: iEEG Multi-Institution Neural Decoding Benchmark

reasons: Explicitly targets the evaluation of 'general-purpose foundation models' for iEEG.
Introduces iMINDBench, a benchmark specifically designed to measure generalization across tasks and institutions for iEEG models.
Evaluates pretrained systems and conducts a scaling study, fitting the criteria for EEG-FM ecosystem papers.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper introduces TriDim, a reusable architectural block that maintains three explicit axes (channel, within-patch time, and across-patch time) to preserve spatial and multi-scale temporal structures in EEG. Unlike conventional models that flatten tokens into a single sequence, TriDim employs cross-axis attention and axis-wise feed-forward networks to coordinate information exchange. Evaluation across eight diverse datasets shows TriDimEEG outperforms 15 baselines, and integrating TriDim blocks into existing foundation models improves accuracy while reducing parameter counts.

headline_results: TriDimEEG outperformed 15 models with a 4.3% relative improvement over EEGDeformer.
Replacing Transformer blocks in 3 foundation models improved accuracy by 7.4% on average and reduced parameters by 17.0% to 47.3%.

key_points: Introduces the TriDim block and TriDimEEG model which explicitly preserve channel, within-patch, and across-patch temporal axes.
Combines cross-axis attention views with axis-wise feed-forward transformations to deeply model interactions between spatial and multi-scale temporal information.
Achieved a 4.3% relative accuracy improvement over the best baseline across 8 datasets and improved 3 foundation models by 7.4% while reducing parameters by up to 47.3%.
limitations: Performance gains vary across tasks, with smaller improvements on datasets like FACED.
The model's superiority over flattened versions is less pronounced on some specific datasets.
Evaluation is limited to the 8 provided benchmarks.

method.architecture: TriDim blocks (cross-axis attention + axis-wise FFN) with a multi-level tri-axis readout.
method.finetuning: Jointly fine-tuned with a classification head.
method.objective: Supervised classification
method.pretraining: Tested by replacing blocks in pretrained models (REVE, CBraMod, CSBrain) using TUH-2K.

summary.one_liner: A structure-preserving EEG decoding block that explicitly models channel, short-term temporal, and long-term temporal axes.
summary.title: Beyond Flattened Tokens: Structure-Preserving EEG Decoding with Reusable TriDim Blocks
summary.unique_contribution: Proposes a reusable 'TriDim' block that preserves three explicit EEG axes (spatial, short-term temporal, and long-term temporal) throughout the backbone to avoid the information loss associated with token flattening.

papers.title: Beyond Flattened Tokens: Structure-Preserving EEG Decoding with Reusable TriDim Blocks

reasons: EEG is the primary modality.
Proposes a reusable architectural block (TriDim) designed to preserve EEG-specific spatial and temporal structures.
Explicitly demonstrates performance gains when replacing blocks in three existing EEG foundation models.
Evaluates the approach across eight diverse EEG datasets, aligning with the ecosystem/adaptation criteria.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes a causal encoder-decoder model trained to map raw binaural acoustic waveforms directly to continuous EEG. Unlike previous models that target specific auditory stages, this foundation model is trained on diverse stimuli (speech, music, tonebursts) to capture physiology across the entire auditory pathway. Evaluation on pABR, speech TRFs, and BIC demonstrates that the model reproduces established human response morphologies and stimulus-dependent effects without task-specific fine-tuning.

headline_results: Predicted waveforms closely resembled human grand averages across multiple auditory paradigms.
Correlations between predicted and actual EEG fell within the range of human subject-level distributions.

key_points: New EEG foundation model: a causal WaveNet-based encoder-decoder that transforms binaural audio into high-sample-rate EEG.
Captures both subcortical and cortical responses, reproducing established effects in pABR, speech TRFs, and binaural interaction components.
Trained on 250 hours of data from 92 subjects using a log-STFT loss to ensure high-frequency accuracy.
limitations: Potential overestimation of neural adaptation or efferent activation effects.
Limited validation of BIC waveforms due to lack of available grand average data.
Training corpus lacks diversity in age and hearing ability.
Subject-specific conditioning effects were not fully analyzed.

method.architecture: Causal WaveNet encoder with a 24-band filterbank, 16-component latent bottleneck, and montage-specific spatial weights.
method.finetuning: None; evaluated in a zero-shot manner using subject-specific conditioning.
method.objective: Log-STFT prediction loss to emphasize higher frequency components of the EEG signal.
method.pretraining: Trained on a large-scale corpus of binaural audio and corresponding EEG recordings.

summary.one_liner: A causal neural network foundation model that predicts high-sample-rate human EEG from binaural audio across subcortical and cortical timescales.
summary.title: A Deep Neural Network for Predicting Continuous Human EEG Across the Auditory Pathway in Response to Sound
summary.unique_contribution: Develops a single audio-to-EEG foundation model capable of predicting auditory electrophysiology across diverse experimental paradigms and neural timescales.

papers.title: A Deep Neural Network for Predicting Continuous Human EEG Across the Auditory Pathway in Response to Sound

reasons: Explicitly claims to present a 'foundation model of human auditory electrophysiology'
Trained on a large-scale dataset of 250 hours of EEG from 92 subjects across diverse stimuli
Demonstrates generalizability across multiple auditory paradigms including ABRs, TRFs, and BIC

summary.detailed_summary: The paper audits LaBraM and CBraMod on motor imagery using a validation-locked protocol to ensure no evaluation labels influence model selection. It finds that supervised models consistently outperform these foundation models on the four-class BCI Competition IV-2a dataset. Furthermore, the authors demonstrate that the impact of input pipelines (broadband vs. narrowband) varies by architecture, suggesting that single-comparator benchmarks may misattribute performance gaps between pretrained and supervised models.

headline_results: Supervised models outperform foundation models on BCI IV-2a.
CBraMod is competitive with supervised models on BNCI2014-004.

key_points: Benchmark of EEG foundation models: Audits LaBraM and CBraMod on motor imagery, finding they are outperformed by supervised baselines on BCI IV-2a.
Methodological insight: Shows that switching to broadband input improves some supervised architectures (ATCNet) while harming others (EEG Conformer).
Calibration finding: Demonstrates that temperature scaling can align foundation model calibration (ECE) with supervised models despite lower accuracy.
limitations: Evaluated only two foundation models out of four attempted.
Only two motor-imagery datasets used.
BNCI2014-004 is not a controlled replication of BCI IV-2a due to different electrode counts.
Subject-level inference limited to nine participants.
Matched-input analysis re-tunes hyperparameters, capturing pipeline plus tuning effects.

method.architecture: Audits LaBraM and CBraMod (Transformers) against supervised baselines (ShallowConvNet, ATCNet, EEG Conformer).
method.finetuning: Validation-locked protocol for learning rate and freeze-depth selection.
method.objective: Frozen probing and fine-tuning for motor imagery classification.
method.pretraining: Utilizes existing pretraining of LaBraM and CBraMod.

summary.one_liner: An audit of EEG foundation models on motor imagery tasks using a leakage-controlled protocol and matched-input analysis.
summary.title: Matched-Input Estimates Differ in Sign Across Architectures: Auditing EEG Foundation Models on Motor Imagery
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a validation-locked evaluation protocol and demonstrates that the effect of input pipelines on performance is architecture-dependent.

papers.title: Matched-Input Estimates Differ in Sign Across Architectures: Auditing EEG Foundation Models on Motor Imagery

reasons: Explicitly audits pretrained EEG foundation models, specifically naming LaBraM and CBraMod.
Focuses on the transferability and performance of EEG-FM representations on downstream motor imagery tasks.
Fits the ecosystem criteria as a benchmark/evaluation paper targeting EEG foundation models.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes Neural State Prediction (NSP), a framework designed to force EEG foundation models to learn distributed neural representations instead of relying on local correlations or positional cues. It achieves this by using an EMA-updated target encoder with identity residualization to remove channel and time-specific biases, and a topology-separated context that masks immediate spatial and temporal neighbors. Pretrained on 2.2 million TUEG segments, NSP outperforms existing baselines on EEG-FM-Bench, achieving 63.94 macro balanced accuracy across 14 datasets.

headline_results: 63.94 macro balanced accuracy (BAC) on EEG-FM-Bench, a 2.35 percentage point improvement over the strongest baseline.

key_points: New EEG foundation model: Neural State Prediction (NSP) uses a latent-predictive objective to learn transferable neural representations.
Obstructs shortcut learning via identity residualization of targets and the exclusion of immediate spatial-temporal neighbors from the context.
Achieves 63.94 macro balanced accuracy on EEG-FM-Bench, surpassing the strongest baseline by 2.35 percentage points.
limitations: Dependence on the quality and diversity of the TUEG dataset for pretraining.
Potential sensitivity to the specific 19-channel mapping when applied to diverse downstream montages.
Computational cost associated with full-parameter multi-task fine-tuning.

method.architecture: Latent-predictive architecture using an EMA-updated Target Encoder and a Context Encoder with 8 CST blocks, width 512, and 8 heads.
method.finetuning: Full-parameter multi-task fine-tuning on downstream EEG-FM-Bench and NeuralBench-EEG-Core datasets.
method.objective: Latent prediction of residualized states of masked regions to prevent shortcut learning.
method.pretraining: Pretrained on 2.2 million EEG segments from the Temple University Hospital EEG Corpus (TUEG).

summary.one_liner: A latent-predictive EEG foundation model that prevents shortcut learning by residualizing target identities and separating spatial-temporal context.
summary.title: Neural State Prediction: Obstructing Shortcut Learning in EEG Foundation Models
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a joint target-context constraint mechanism using identity residualization and topology-separated masking to obstruct shortcut learning in EEG latent prediction.

papers.title: Neural State Prediction: Obstructing Shortcut Learning in EEG Foundation Models

reasons: Explicitly targets the improvement of EEG foundation models and transferable neural representations.
Proposes a new pretraining framework (NSP) trained on a large-scale dataset of 2.2 million EEG segments.
Evaluates the model across 30 diverse downstream EEG datasets and utilizes EEG-FM-Bench.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes EEG-Arena, an open-source evaluation framework designed to systematically assess the transferability and scaling properties of EEG foundation models (FMs). By conducting over 20,000 evaluations across 23 public datasets and 57 tasks, the authors compare 30 FMs against 25 supervised baselines. The results demonstrate that while pretraining generally improves downstream performance and data scaling yields sustained gains, there is no consistent positive relationship between model parameter count and performance.

summary.detailed_summary: ERP-FM is a lightweight Transformer-based foundation model pretrained on over 1.5 million single-trial ERPs from 3,696 subjects across 38 datasets. It utilizes single-channel tokenization with fine-grained temporal resolution and a mixed masked autoencoding objective to capture transient ERP dynamics. Evaluation across 12 downstream datasets for event and disease classification shows that ERP-FM outperforms 17 existing methods, demonstrating the effectiveness of combining single-trial pretraining with averaged-trial adaptation.

Top-1 performance in 20 of 36 dataset-metric evaluations

Method novelty: Utilizes mixed masked autoencoding and fine-grained temporal tokenization (0.25s patches) to better capture transient ERP dynamics.
Strong evidence: Achieved the best overall average rank across 12 downstream datasets, with Top-1 performance in 20 of 36 dataset-metric evaluations.
limitations: Not explicitly discussed in the provided text
Potential scalability limits due to the lightweight architecture

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes a formal three-parameter framework to unify EEG masking strategies, conducting a controlled grid sweep of 29 spatio-temporal configurations across MAE and JEPA SSL frameworks. By evaluating 58 pre-trained models on 12 OpenEEGBench datasets via linear probing, the authors identify a shared optimum at moderate spatial radii and short temporal lengths. The study also characterizes a novel 'bias-inflation collapse' specific to JEPA on multichannel signals and demonstrates that optimized masking can achieve REVE-level performance with significantly less compute.

headline_results: Optimal performance achieved with moderate spatial radius and short temporal length
JEPA exhibits bias-inflation collapse on multichannel data

key_points: Methodological study on EEG foundation models: systematically ablates spatio-temporal masking geometries across MAE and JEPA frameworks.
Identifies an optimal masking regime (moderate spatial radius, short temporal length) and a JEPA-specific 'bias-inflation collapse' failure mode.
Demonstrates that a well-chosen mask allows the pipeline to reach REVE-level performance using only a fraction of the pre-training compute.
limitations: Evaluation is limited to linear probing on frozen features rather than full fine-tuning.
The study uses a fixed mask ratio of 0.55, though the authors claim results hold across ratios.
The backbone is fixed to REVE-Small, though robustness was tested in the appendix.
The JEPA framework was tested without auxiliary anti-collapse losses to maintain parity with MAE.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper addresses the risk of assigning false physiological meanings to Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) latents in EEG foundation models, specifically showing that apparent frequency-sensitivity is often an artifact of signal distortion. The authors introduce a 'validation ladder' that requires latents to pass distortion control, specificity tests, and independent observational validation before being labeled as representing a physiological property. Testing across 27 settings (3 backbones, 3 datasets, 3 depths) reveals that a strong raw response to alpha-band removal collapses after normalizing for removed spectral energy, suggesting that many 'interpretable' features are actually just detecting signal corruption.

headline_results: Alpha-sensitive latents failed distortion-controlled selectivity across all 27 settings
Normalized firing change ratio dropped from 7.3x to 0.28x after spectral energy control

key_points: Method for SAE interpretability: Proposes a validation ladder to rigorously verify whether SAE latents in EEG foundation models represent actual physiological properties.
Evidence of misinterpretation: Demonstrates that a 7.3x raw response to alpha-band removal in 27 different settings drops to 0.28x after controlling for removed spectral energy.
Validation failure: Shows that latents selected for alpha-sensitivity often anti-correlate with relative alpha power on clean EEG and lack preferential importance for task readouts.
limitations: Remaining settings used only one SAE seed
Readout groups were unmatched on baseline activity for ablation tests
Relative band power tests only assess global frequency readings
Task-readout analysis covered only 21 of 27 settings due to unavailable exports
Band-stop filtering cannot fully isolate biological oscillators
Relevance was defined using a simple logistic probe on mean-pooled codes

summary.detailed_summary: PhysioTRACE is a four-axis behavioral audit (Recover, Stress, Intervene, Verify) designed to determine if frozen encoders in physiological foundation models rely on recording conditions (provenance) rather than actual physiology for task prediction. It separates what a probe can decode from what a task head actually uses by reversing provenance-target associations and attempting to remove localized provenance components. The framework was validated on EEG and ECG models, demonstrating that provenance decodability does not consistently predict out-of-distribution utility and providing a method to certify remedies for identified shortcuts.

headline_results: Detected 0.2 AUROC loss on known EEG shortcuts
Certified remedy removing 91% of excess vulnerability in one ECG model

key_points: Benchmark for physiological foundation models: PhysioTRACE provides a four-axis behavioral audit to detect and remedy reliance on acquisition provenance shortcuts.
Methodological novelty: It uses a 'Stress' axis to reverse provenance-target associations and a 'Verify' axis to certify the removal of provenance components without losing task utility.
Concrete evidence: On paired EEG views, it detected a known shortcut (0.2 AUROC loss) and certified a rank-two component removal that restored control-level behavior.
limitations: The audit requires the ability to reverse provenance-target associations, which may be difficult in some real-world datasets.
The 'Verify' step relies on a declared utility margin, which may be subjective.
The method focuses on frozen encoders and linear heads, potentially missing shortcuts in non-linear heads.
The effectiveness of the remedy depends on the provenance being low-rank or localized.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper evaluates the personal adaptation of three frozen EEG foundation models (CBraMod, REVE, and LaBraM) using 235 subjects across multiple motor-imagery datasets. It demonstrates that while personal adapters (LoRA/FiLM) consistently outperform population models and swapped adapters, these gains diminish as the population model's training budget increases. Furthermore, the study finds that few-label calibration, unlabeled context, and meta-learning are unreliable methods for recovering these personalization benefits.

headline_results: Personal adapters improved mean BA by 1.5-5.4 pp over population and 2.3-7.3 pp over exchanged adapters.

key_points: Methodological study on EEG-FM calibration: evaluates how to separate personal adaptation gains from population-level improvements using dual-contrast benchmarks.
Demonstrates that personal adapters (LoRA/FiLM) provide a consistent boost (1.5-7.3 pp) over population and swapped baselines, though the effect size shrinks with more population training.
Finds that 'cheap' calibration strategies, including meta-learning and unlabeled context, fail to reliably recover personalization benefits.
limitations: Limited to binary motor imagery tasks.
Evaluation restricted to within-session calibration.
Small cohort size for the BNCI dataset.
Channel-restricted readout for the Lee dataset.
Differences in preprocessing and pretraining sources limit attribution of results to the backbone alone.
Subject-bootstrap intervals are pointwise and conditional on selected checkpoints.

summary.detailed_summary: PHASE proposes a two-stage foundation model consisting of a temporal stage (PHASE-T) and a spatiotemporal stage (PHASE-ST) that use measurable physiological properties as explicit learning targets. Unlike prior models that rely on implicit reconstruction, PHASE pairs masked latent prediction with targets like multi-scale wavelet power and cross-channel synchrony. Evaluation on the Omni-iEEG benchmark shows that frozen PHASE-T outperforms existing foundation models by up to 31%, while fine-tuned versions set a new state-of-the-art across clinical tasks.

headline_results: Frozen PHASE-T outperformed other foundation models by up to 31% on Omni-iEEG.
Fine-tuned PHASE-T surpassed task-specific supervised models on clinical tasks.
Superior performance on BrainTreebank auditory decoding compared to published models.

key_points: New EEG foundation model: PHASE uses a two-stage hierarchical architecture (PHASE-T and PHASE-ST) to explicitly learn physiological targets instead of relying solely on implicit signal reconstruction.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance on Omni-iEEG clinical tasks and superior auditory decoding on BrainTreebank, outperforming task-specific models when fine-tuned.
Demonstrates strong generalization to unseen institutions and the ability to encapsulate anatomical and pathological characteristics without explicit labels during pretraining.
limitations: Pretraining is sequential (temporal then spatial) rather than joint.
Temporal context is limited to one-minute windows.
Dependencies across separate recording windows are not explicitly modeled.
Evaluation is limited to a specific set of clinical and auditory tasks.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes a joint functional and representational framework to evaluate the robustness of four EEG foundation models (SingLEM, CBraMod, LUNA, and REVE) to changes in electrode montages. Unlike previous work focusing primarily on downstream performance, this study dissociates representational similarity from functional stability using linear probes and Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA). Results on resting-state and motor-imagery tasks demonstrate that montage robustness is a joint property of the encoder and its aggregation method, with anatomically aligned ROI pooling significantly outperforming learned global readouts.

headline_results: ROI pooling is more robust than learned global readouts
Representational stability does not imply functional stability

key_points: Benchmark study: Evaluates the impact of electrode montage changes on the representations and predictions of four state-of-the-art EEG foundation models.
Findings reveal a dissociation between representational similarity and functional stability, meaning stable embeddings do not guarantee stable downstream performance.
Identifies that ROI-based aggregation is significantly more robust to channel reduction than learned global readouts.
limitations: Cross-model patterns are consistent with hypotheses but do not identify exact causes.
Models differ in pretraining data and size, making it hard to isolate the effect of channel-fusion alone.
Preprocessing was matched to pretraining configurations, which may limit the attribution of differences to architecture.
